items.title: using uv workspaces in flat layouts (e.g. monorepos)
items.reason: Closest layout discussion: a maintainer recommends a project-less virtual workspace root in the siblings' common parent. It does not support one sibling acting as the root for another.

items.title: Are doubly-nested packages supported in a workspace?
items.reason: Shows the same root-discovery failure and `workspace = true` not-a-member error, but all members are descendants of the root behind an intervening project, not outside it.

items.title: Add `workspace_dir` to `tool.uv.sources`
items.reason: Requested dependency lookup in another workspace and established an alternative for separate workspace trees; it did not request shared membership.

items.title: Allow `workspace` to take a path in `tool.uv.sources`
items.reason: Implemented path-valued workspace sources, explicitly without reusing the external workspace lockfile. It does not implement external members or shared workspace state.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests. Literal searches covered `workspace members outside`, `outside workspace root`, `../` with `workspace = true`, `No workspace root found`, and the exact not-a-workspace-member error. Conceptual searches covered sibling/external members, flat monorepos, parent-directory members, root discovery, root overrides, and cross-workspace dependencies. Fix-oriented searches followed relative-path and workspace-discovery issue chains. astral-sh/uv#16285 and astral-sh/uv#16296 were ruled out because they concern leading `./` paths below the root; astral-sh/uv#16640 and astral-sh/uv#17156 concern nested projects or conflicting nested-workspace sources.

type_reason: The implementation explicitly defines workspace members as being below their root and discovers a member's workspace by traversing ancestor directories. Supporting a sibling outside that root requires a new workspace layout and discovery capability, rather than correcting behavior promised by the current model. No existing item tracks that same capability.
summary: No existing issue or pull request tracks true workspace members outside their root. The closest discussion recommends a common virtual root for flat siblings, while a merged feature supports dependency lookup into a separate workspace without shared membership or lockfile semantics.
draft_response:
uv currently expects workspace members to be below the workspace root, and member-side discovery walks ancestor directories. That is why `b` cannot discover a workspace rooted at its sibling `a` in this layout.

For a single shared workspace, the supported layout is a project-less `pyproject.toml` in `example/` with `members = ["a", "b"]`, as discussed in astral-sh/uv#13589. If the projects should remain separate workspaces, astral-sh/uv#18401 added path-valued workspace sources, so `b` can use `a = { workspace = "../a" }`; that resolves from the other workspace but does not make `b` a member of `a` or share its lockfile.

We'll treat allowing `../b` as a true member as a separate enhancement.
